name: Pointillism
summary: A picture made of small, separate dots of pure colour that the eye mixes at a distance. The scene is still and ordered, built by colour theory and not by blending.

philosophy.core_thesis: Colour is a science: pure dots set side by side mix in the eye with more light than a mix on the palette, and a picture can be built by rule.
design_principles: Lay each dot as a separate touch of pure colour, 2–5mm across, with a ground that shows between them.
Mix by juxtaposition: set complementary pairs, such as orange and blue, next to each other, so that the eye fuses them.
Build each area from 3 elements: local colour, light (warm) and shadow (cool complement), plus a reflected colour.
Hold the scene in still, simple masses: a frieze of figures in profile and in full face, in a clear, ordered space.
Plan the picture on a grid or a golden-section armature, with strong verticals and horizontals.
Add a painted border in the colour that contrasts with the edge of the scene.
Use a matt, chalky surface so that the dots stay pure and bright.
anti_patterns: Blended or glazed colour that hides the dot
Soft, lost edges that run into the next form
Movement, blur and a fleeting moment
Large flat areas of one mixed colour

composition.layout: A still, ordered arrangement of simple masses on a hidden grid of verticals and horizontals, with a frieze of figures at the front and a horizon at 40–50% of the height.
composition.focal_point: A figure or a mass at one third from an edge, set by the golden section at 0.62 of the width or the height.
composition.format: A wide canvas at 3:2 to 2:1; a painted border of 20–60mm in a dot-built contrast colour closes the picture.

principles.rule: Divide the canvas by the golden section at 0.62, and set the main vertical and the horizon on those lines.
Repeat a small unit, such as a figure, a tree or a parasol, 6–10 times at a regular step of 8–12% of the picture width.
Use a quiet, formal pose: figures in strict profile or full face, with a vertical axis in each figure and none for the whole picture.
Split every area into 3 dot colours: a local hue at 60%, a warm light hue at 25%, and a cool shadow hue at 15%.
Hold the dot size to 2–5mm across the whole picture, and vary only the hue and value of the dot.
Close the picture with a painted border of 20–60mm, in a hue that is the complement of the nearby edge.

palette.strategy: Pure spectral hues set in dots, with complementary pairs in contact; no black and no earth, and the mix happens in the eye.
palette.distribution: A broad light and sky area 30–40%, local colour of the subject 30–40%, a cool shadow colour 15–20%, and a warm light colour 10–15%.
palette.ground: A white or very pale ground that shows between the dots and lifts the colour.

colours.name: Cadmium orange
colours.role: warm light, the complement of blue

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Oil paint, thick and matt, used straight from the tube with little medium.
brushwork_and_medium.support: A fine canvas with a white ground.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: Small, round dots or short touches of 2–5mm, laid in regular rows, one dab at a time; 10 000 or more dots on a large canvas.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: One layer of dots, with a second pass of 1–2 corrections; no blending and no glaze.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: A hard form edge made by a change in the dot hue; a slight vibration, with no line drawn.

light_and_modelling.light: A bright, even daylight, shown by warm yellow-orange dots in the lit areas and cool blue-violet dots in the shadow.
light_and_modelling.modelling: By the change of the dot hue and value in 3–4 steps; the form is built by colour and not by line.
light_and_modelling.shadow: A cool, coloured shadow of blue, violet or green dots at value 40–60%; no black.
light_and_modelling.temperature: A warm lit area against a cool shadow, with the complement set side by side so that the edge vibrates.

subject.typical: Leisure in a park or on a river, a harbour, a bather, a circus, a seaside and a town scene.
subject.figure_scale: Small to medium figures at 15–45% of the picture height, seen in profile or full face.
subject.treatment: Calm, frozen and modern; people stand and sit as in a frieze, with no story and no sign of emotion.

surface.texture: A fine, regular grain of dots across the whole picture, with the canvas weave in view.

works.work: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884
Oil Sketch for "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884"

reference_works.note: Object ids were checked against the Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data). The oil sketch shows the dot method at a small size. Look at the museum page for the image and its licence.

emotion.target_response: Calm, clear attention: the viewer sees a quiet, ordered scene that shimmers as the eye mixes the dots.

use_cases: poster and cover with a luminous, dotted texture
avoid_when: The brief needs a fast, loose or spontaneous mood.
The picture must show sharp fine detail, such as a face or a product label.

modifiers.how: Keep the bright colour and the open-air light; make the touch a quick dab or dash of 10–20mm, allow blending at the edges, and drop the grid.
Keep the pure hue; enlarge the dot to a patch of 20–60mm, allow a hue that is not true to nature, and add a dark contour.
